skill.name: product-photography
skill.description: Create AI product photography prompts and workflows for studio packshots, hero shots, lifestyle scenes, detail images, and e-commerce image sets.

skill.author: halt-catch-fire

security_audit.summary: The skill is a product photography guide that intentionally relies on the belt CLI and external image-generation services. Most static hits are Markdown fence false positives, but real CLI execution, external install commands, hardcoded service links, and possible upload of local product images remain relevant risks.

remediation.suggestion: State clearly that belt commands send prompts, job metadata, and possibly assets to third-party model services. Recommend reviewing vendor terms before use.
Pin installation guidance to a reviewed release or checksum where possible, and warn users before running npx or remote install steps.

remediation.issue: Local image inputs may contain confidential product assets
remediation.suggestion: Add a privacy note advising users not to upload unreleased products, customer data, trademarks, or confidential images without approval.

content.value_statement: Product teams need consistent e-commerce images without planning every shot. This skill provides product photography prompt patterns, shot lists, lighting guidance, and workflow examples.
actual_capabilities: Provides prompt examples for hero shots, packshots, lifestyle scenes, scale shots, detail shots, and group images.
Explains camera angles, lighting setups, shadow types, and background choices for product photography.
Outlines a 7 to 9 image e-commerce listing set with recommended image order.
Gives category-specific guidance for food, jewelry, electronics, cosmetics, apparel, and fashion products.
Shows belt CLI examples for generation, image editing, and image upscaling workflows.
Identifies common product photography mistakes and practical fixes.
limitations: Requires the belt CLI and access to supported external image model apps.
Does not verify marketplace policy compliance for every platform or product category.
Generated images may need manual review for brand accuracy, product fidelity, and legal clearance.
Image editing examples assume users already have suitable source images and permissions.

use_cases.title: Build a Marketplace Listing Image Set
use_cases.description: Create prompts for a complete e-commerce listing, including primary packshot, lifestyle, detail, scale, and alternate angle images.

use_cases.title: Plan Brand Campaign Product Visuals
use_cases.description: Translate product positioning into hero images with appropriate background, lighting, props, and composition choices.

use_cases.title: Create Consistent Product Variants
use_cases.description: Use shared prompt structure and category rules to generate images for multiple products in one visual style.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Packshot
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a clean e-commerce packshot prompt for [product]. Use a pure white background, soft even lighting, sharp focus, and marketplace-ready composition.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Lifestyle Scene
prompt_templates.scenario: Context image for a product page
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a lifestyle product photography prompt for [product] used by [customer type] in [setting]. Include lighting, props, mood, and composition.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Full Listing Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 7 image product listing plan for [product]. Include image purpose, shot type, background, angle, lighting, and prompt text for each image.

prompt_templates.title: Refine a Brand-Specific Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a product photography workflow for [brand] and [product line]. Maintain a consistent visual system across hero, detail, lifestyle, scale, and collection images.

output_examples.input: A seller needs a primary image for a leather wallet listing.
output_examples.output: A white-background packshot direction with upright wallet placement, slight angle, soft even studio light, sharp texture detail, and no props.

output_examples.input: A beauty brand needs lifestyle images for skincare bottles.
output_examples.output: A marble-surface flat lay concept with soft pastel styling, minimal props, clean editorial lighting, and coordinated bottle arrangement.

output_examples.input: A tech team needs a premium hero image for headphones.
output_examples.output: A dramatic hero shot direction with rim lighting, clean gradient background, subtle reflection, three-quarter angle, and crisp material detail.

best_practices: Start with the product category, target platform, and required image size before writing prompts.
Keep lighting, background family, and camera angle consistent across a product image set.
Review every generated image for product accuracy, text artifacts, logo issues, and marketplace policy fit.
anti_patterns: Do not use busy props or backgrounds that compete with the product.
Do not rely on generated images without checking dimensions, materials, labels, and brand details.
Do not upload confidential product images to external services without approval.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create AI prompts and workflows for product packshots, hero images, lifestyle scenes, detail shots, and listing image sets.

faq.question: Does it generate images by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and command examples for using external image-generation apps through the belt CLI.

faq.question: Can I use it for Amazon listing images?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes white background packshot guidance and common marketplace requirements, but you should confirm current platform rules.

faq.question: Can it help with different product categories?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for food, jewelry, electronics, beauty products, apparel, and fashion use cases.

faq.question: What should I review before publishing images?
faq.answer: Check product fidelity, brand details, text artifacts, image size, background requirements, and legal rights for all visible assets.

faq.question: Is there a privacy concern?
faq.answer: Yes. Some workflows may send prompts or image files to external services, so avoid confidential assets unless approved.
